source.title: A Comprehensive Survey and Performance Analysis of Activation Functions in Deep Learning
source.authors: S. Dubey; S. Singh; B. Chaudhuri

record.file_problem: Full text is present. The title in the supplied text differs slightly from the catalog title; it is the same activation-functions survey and benchmark.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains CNNs with different activation functions and reports CIFAR-100 training-loss convergence results. It does not measure the training classification error named by V1, or test the specific conditions in V2–V6.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 tables report test accuracy, not training classification error. Training-convergence results are reported for CIFAR-100; initialization details are not stated. The initialization discussion in Section 8 and results cited from other papers are not this study's own experimental results.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks activation functions, but its own results do not test V1–V6. It reports test accuracy and qualitative training-loss convergence, without training classification error or controlled comparisons of width, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization. Section 8 discusses initialization findings from other studies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: activation suitability varies with the network and task. The authors additionally emphasize convergence and computational-cost tradeoffs, reporting good convergence for PAU, PReLU, and PDELU while identifying PDELU and SRS as computationally expensive.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares activation functions in CNN training; it does not test the original claim's intervention or measure training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Training convergence differs by activation function and model; SRS diverges with SENet18, while sigmoid and Elliott are described as having the poorest convergence overall.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-100, PAU converges fastest in most tested cases; PReLU, GELU, and PDELU show consistently good convergence; SRS diverges with SENet18; sigmoid and Elliott have the poorest convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With the tested CNNs and Adam training recipe, activation choice affects training-loss convergence, and some activation-model combinations diverge.

record.peer_reviewed: Neurocomputing; paper states it is accepted, copyright to be transferred to Elsevier.
record.problems: Training-convergence results are qualitative in the text and refer to Figure 3; no training classification-error values are reported. Initialization details are not stated. Five trials and standard deviations are reported for the accuracy tables, but not for the convergence statements.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 test-accuracy results are not rows because they do not measure the claim's training-error outcome. The figure's model-specific loss curves are not transcribed as separate rows because the supplied text gives no figure values or model-specific descriptions beyond the stated aggregate and SENet18/SRS result.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error from random initialization, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with increasing depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient preservation, orthogonality, and convolution-kernel initialization on learning speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, divergence thresholds, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including the Fixup alternative.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows and its assessment that all six versions are untested. Figure 3's curves are not readable in the supplied text; their omission is already declared in rows_left_out. The conclusion's statement about improper initialization causing divergence is not backed here by an initialization comparison.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model-size comparisons, or early stopping.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or width sweep.
No controlled depth comparison of plain and shortcut networks or normalization ablation.
No initialization comparison or test of trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability or sharpness experiment.

rows.subject: Different CNN models (MobileNet, VGG16, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, SENet18, and DenseNet121; aggregate finding)
rows.operation_detail: Compared CIFAR-100 training-loss convergence across activation functions.
rows.value: PAU has the fastest convergence in most cases.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative statement across models; the text does not specify which model cases.
rows.check: The qualitative finding is accurately extracted, but faster convergence after changing activation functions does not establish any version's effect. No initialization comparison or near-zero training classification error is reported.

rows.subject: Different CNN models (MobileNet, VGG16, GoogLeNet, ResNet50, SENet18, and DenseNet121; aggregate finding)
rows.operation_detail: Compared CIFAR-100 training-loss convergence across activation functions.
rows.value: PReLU, GELU, and PDELU are described as consistent with good convergence.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative statement; no model-specific values are given in the text.
rows.check: The qualitative finding is accurately extracted. Good convergence for these activations does not measure any named version; 'observed' has no applicable claim effect here.

rows.subject: SENet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SRS activation on CIFAR100.
rows.note: The text explicitly identifies this model and activation combination as diverging.
rows.check: SENet18 with SRS explicitly diverges, but this does not establish a reversal of any version. Training classification error, initialization conditions, and learning-rate stability thresholds are not reported.

rows.subject: Different CNN models (aggregate finding)
rows.operation_detail: Compared CIFAR-100 training-loss convergence across activation functions.
rows.value: Sigmoid and Elliott showed the poorest convergence.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative comparison; the text does not specify model-specific values.
rows.check: The authors describe sigmoid and Elliott as having the poorest convergence. This relative ranking does not establish partial occurrence of any named version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
